question: On which date in 1991 was the Indian rupee devalued?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1st July**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

The Indian rupee was devalued in 1991 in two phases:

 
• **July 1, 1991:** The rupee was devalued by approximately 9%.
 
• **July 3, 1991:** The rupee was further devalued by approximately 11%.

 
• The 1991 devaluation occurred during a severe economic crisis in India.
 
• India was facing a balance of payments crisis, with dwindling foreign exchange reserves.
 
• The crisis was exacerbated by factors such as the Gulf War, which led to increased oil prices and a decline in remittances.
 
• The devaluation of the rupee was a key measure taken to address the crisis.
 
• The goal was to make Indian exports more competitive and to attract foreign investment.
 
• The devaluation was part of a broader set of economic reforms initiated by the government of Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao and Finance Minister Manmohan Singh.
 
• These reforms aimed to liberalize the Indian economy and to reduce government control.
 
• The devaluation was a significant policy shift, as it marked a move away from a fixed exchange rate system.
 
• The move was also designed to increase the amount of foreign currency coming into India.
 
• The 1991 economic crisis and the subsequent reforms had a profound impact on the Indian economy.
 
• It was a major turning point for the economic policies of India.
 
• The devaluation was a very difficult, but ultimately necessary action.
 
• The result of the devaluation, and other economic reforms, lead to a large growth in the Indian economy in the following years.
 
• The reforms helped to integrate India into the global economy.
 
• The events of 1991 are considered to be a watershed moment in India's economic history.
 
• The actions taken in 1991 helped to set India on a path of economic growth.
 
• The 1991 crisis and reforms are studied by economists around the world.
 
• The events of that time period are still very relevant to the current Indian economy.
 
• The reserve bank of India, played a very important role in the devaluation process.
